screening_decisions.reason: Primary case-control study assessing VTE risk in women using low-estrogen combined oral contraceptives. Meets population, intervention, and outcome criteria.
Prospective cohort study evaluating VTE risk factors, including oral contraceptive use in women. Provides relevant data on COC and VTE association.
Study outcome focuses on coagulation system parameters (factors V, VII, VIII, etc.) rather than clinical venous thrombosis events.
Hospital-based case-control study assessing VTE risk in relation to recent oral contraceptive use. Meets all selection criteria.
Case-control study specifically designed to assess VTE risk in nonpredisposed women using oral contraceptives while minimizing detection bias. Meets criteria.
Methodological paper on statistical models for network meta-analysis. Does not involve the target population or clinical outcomes.
Review article discussing thrombophilias and hormone use. Not a primary study evaluating COC and VTE risk in healthy women.
Case-control study investigating the association between oral contraceptive use and venous thromboembolism. Meets selection criteria.
Consensus statement/survey evaluating scientific data and making prescription recommendations. Not a primary research study.
Review compiling incidence estimates from various studies. Does not present primary data on COC users and VTE.
Nested case-control study using GPRD data to compare VTE risk between third- and second-generation COCs. Meets criteria.
Matched case-control study assessing VTE risk in women using gestodene-containing COCs versus other progestins. Meets criteria.
Study modeling relative risk of mortality from VTE in oral contraceptive users. Relevant to the COC-VTE outcome relationship.
Database case-control study comparing VTE risk between second- and third-generation COC users. Meets criteria.
Examines methodological biases in VTE-OC studies but also presents primary data on OC use and VTE risk (including idiopathic VTE). Included conservatively.
Cohort and nested case-control study assessing VTE risk in women using third-generation COCs vs levonorgestrel COCs. Meets criteria.
Large national registry-based cohort study assessing VTE risk by progestogen type and estrogen dose in COC users. Meets criteria.
National case-control study estimating relative risk of fatal pulmonary embolism (a VT outcome) in women using combined oral contraceptives. Meets criteria.
Pharmacovigilance study analyzing spontaneous reports of cardiovascular reactions, including venous thrombosis, associated with different COC formulations. Included conservatively.
Danish case-control study investigating VTE risk in women using oral contraceptives. Meets population, intervention, and outcome criteria.
Study assesses the association between oral contraceptive use and venous thromboembolism in healthy women aged 15-44, meeting all selection criteria.
Evaluates the risk of VTE in women aged 15-44 using different generations of oral contraceptives, aligning with the criteria.
Nested case-control study estimating idiopathic VTE risk in women using various COC formulations.
Methodological paper on mixed treatment comparisons using rheumatoid arthritis drug examples; does not involve COC or VT in women.
Focuses on VTE risk among young, healthy women using second- vs third-generation oral contraceptives.
Primary aim is validating a diagnostic test for APC resistance in men and women with thrombophilia; COC use is only a secondary stratification factor.
Hospital-based case-control study evaluating the association between oral contraceptive use and VTE/PE in women.
Examines the interaction between oral contraceptive use and thrombophilic mutations on VTE risk in women of reproductive age.
Nested case-control study assessing nonfatal VTE risk in women using different progestin-containing oral contraceptives.
Retrospective study determining incidences of fatal VTE in relation to different COC types in women aged 15-44.
Cochrane review focusing on contraceptive effectiveness, bleeding patterns, and side effects; venous thrombosis is not the primary outcome.
Clinical practice guideline for diagnosing DVT/PE; not an original study on COC use and VT.
Review article on the general epidemiology of VTE; does not focus on COC use as an exposure.
Population-based study estimating incidence and mortality of VT in a general population; does not assess COC use.
Large case-control study assessing venous thrombosis risk associated with different estrogen doses and progestogen types in premenopausal women.
National cohort study evaluating VTE risk in women using different types of hormonal contraception, including COCs.
Diagnostic accuracy study evaluating a clinical model for DVT; does not investigate COC use or VT outcomes.
Review of the natural history, resolution, and recurrence of VTE; does not focus on COC exposure.
Cohort study assessing the dose-response relationship between oral contraceptive estrogen content and venous thromboembolism in women.
Case-control study identifying risk factors for DVT, specifically highlighting minidose oral contraception as a major risk factor in non-menopausal women.
This is a clinical review article, not a primary study. It discusses both hormonal contraceptives and HRT, and does not present original data on healthy women taking COC with VT as outcome.
Cohort study of women aged 12-50 using combined oral contraceptives with venous thrombotic events (DVT and PE) as outcome. Meets all selection criteria.
This study focuses on lifestyle factors (exercise, smoking, alcohol) and VTE risk, not on COC use. COC is not the intervention being studied.
Uses spontaneous reporting data to estimate VTE incidence for different COCs. Studies women taking COCs with VT as outcome.
This is a review article describing pharmacological profiles of progestins. No primary data on VT outcomes in women taking COCs.
Study includes both males and females, and focuses on adolescent PE epidemiology. Not specifically about healthy women taking COC with VT as primary outcome.
Studies 72 women with acute thromboembolic diseases, 34 of whom were using hormonal contraceptives. Examines link between hormonal contraceptive use and thromboembolic diseases.
Focuses on post-thrombotic syndrome predictors after DVT, not on COC use. Does not study women taking COCs with VT as outcome.
Assesses VT risk in women using oral contraceptives. Includes evaluation of thrombophilias but primarily studies OC use and VT outcome.
Case-control study comparing VTE risk in women using different OCs. Women aged 15-44 with idiopathic VTE. Meets selection criteria.
This is a review article examining epidemiologic studies and discussing controversies. Not a primary study with original data.
Outcome is hemostasis variables, not venous thrombosis events. Does not meet the VT outcome criterion.
Studies 28 women with OC-induced venous thrombosis at different ages. Examines OC use and VT outcome, though some women have prothrombotic conditions.
Case-control study of 148 women with DVT and 277 healthy controls. Examines interaction between genetic mutations and OC use with DVT as outcome.
Case-control study examining VTE risk factors including oral contraceptive pill use in Thai women. Studies women with VTE and OC use.
Focuses on protein C deficiency and venous thromboembolism in blood donors. Not about COC use as intervention.
Studies OC initiators with thromboembolism outcome. Examines residual confounding in a cohort of women using OCs with thromboembolism as outcome.
Analyzes spontaneous reports of thromboembolism from UK, Sweden, Denmark for different OC preparations. Studies women using OCs with VT outcome.
Case-control study of women under 50 examining OC use and smoking effects on DVT and PE. Meets selection criteria.
Appears to be a review article from NEJM summarizing historical observations and studies. Not a primary study with original data.

Case-control study of women aged 15-49 years examining VTE risk associated with different COC formulations (dienogest, drospirenone vs levonorgestrel). Meets criteria: healthy women taking COC with VTE as outcome.

Retrospective case-reference study of women aged 15-44 years examining VTE incidence among COC users. Reports VTE rates by COC type (third generation vs other COCs). Meets criteria: women taking COC with VTE as outcome.

Matched case-control study in 10 centers (Germany/UK) of women aged 16-44 years with VTE vs controls without VTE. Compares VTE risk across different COC generations and progestagen types. Meets criteria: women taking COC with VTE as outcome.

Review article discussing pharmacological properties of new progestins. No primary study data on VTE outcomes; hypothesis about neutral effects on vascular risks needs confirmation in clinical trials. Does not meet criteria: no actual VTE outcome data.

Randomized study measuring hemostasis biomarkers (F1+2, PAP, D-dimer, protein S, etc.) not actual VTE events. Outcome is coagulation markers, not venous thrombosis. Does not meet criteria: VT not measured as outcome.
Review paper on APC resistance mechanisms and etiology. Not a primary study on COC use and VTE. Does not meet criteria: no COC-VTE study data.

Case-control study of women aged 15-49 years with first episode of venous thrombosis vs controls. Examines VTE risk with low-dose OCs while controlling for bias. Meets criteria: women taking COC with VTE as outcome.
Brief editorial/commentary on observational studies vs randomized trials. No specific study on COC and VTE. Does not meet criteria: no relevant study data.
Methodological paper on bias assessment in non-randomised studies. Not a primary study on COC and VTE. Does not meet criteria: methodological review, not COC-VTE study.

Cohort study comparing thromboembolism risk between ethinylestradiol/drospirenone initiators vs other OC initiators. Medical record-confirmed thromboembolism cases. Meets criteria: women taking COC with thromboembolism as outcome.

Nested case-control analysis of UK GP records examining VTE risk with different COC formulations (desogestrel, gestodene vs levonorgestrel). Verified cases of idiopathic VTE. Meets criteria: women taking COC with VTE as outcome.

Case-control study of premenopausal women aged 15-49 with DVT vs population controls. Examines interaction between COC use and factor V Leiden mutation on VTE risk. While includes women with genetic thrombophilia, also reports overall COC-VTE risk. Conservative approach: INCLUDE for potential relevance.
Methodological paper on funnel plot asymmetry for detecting bias in meta-analyses. Not a primary study on COC and VTE. Does not meet criteria: methodological paper, not COC-VTE study.

Study examining multiple vascular disease risk factors in women including oral contraceptive use and venous thromboembolism. Reports that OC use was associated with increased VTE risk. Meets criteria: women taking COC with VTE as outcome.

Prospective cohort study of women aged 30-55 examining PE risk with current/past OC use and postmenopausal hormones. PE is a form of venous thromboembolism. Meets criteria: women taking COC with VT (PE) as outcome.

Cohort study of women aged 18-46 comparing VTE risk between drospirenone and levonorgestrel COCs, stratified by EE dosage. Large sample size with VTE defined by ICD coding and anticoagulation. Meets criteria: women taking COC with VTE as outcome.

Descriptive epidemiology of hospitalization rates for cardiovascular/thromboembolic events in Austrian women. No comparison of COC users vs non-users; no examination of COC-VTE association. Does not meet criteria: no COC-VTE risk assessment.

Controlled prospective survey testing hypothesis that anovulants (oral contraceptives) increase thromboembolic disease incidence. Examines superficial venous thrombosis and deep-vein thrombosis. Meets criteria: women taking COC with thrombosis as outcome.

Study of thrombophilia risk factors in extrahepatic portal vein obstruction (EHPVO), not typical venous thromboembolism. States 'oral contraceptive use was not associated with increased risk of EHPVO'. Different outcome (portal vein vs systemic VTE). Does not meet criteria: wrong VT outcome type.

Study objective explicitly states determination of VTE risk with anti-androgen oral contraceptives containing cyproterone acetate and ethinyloestradiol. Limited abstract but clearly addresses COC-VTE relationship. Conservative approach: INCLUDE pending full text review.
Prospective cohort study of new OC users (DRSP, LNG, other progestins) with venous thromboembolism as outcome. Population appears to be healthy women initiating contraception.
Study focuses on women over 50 years old, many likely postmenopausal. This population differs from typical healthy reproductive-age women taking COCs for contraception.
Descriptive overview article about pill usage statistics. No primary research data, no VT outcomes assessed.
Review article discussing pharmacogenetic aspects of OC use and thrombosis risk. Not primary research with original data.
Cohort and case-control analyses of VTE risk in women prescribed CPA/EE. While some women have acne/hirsutism/PCOS, these are common conditions and study assesses COC-VT association.
Population-based case-control study testing oral contraceptives as independent VTE risk factors. Includes healthy women with objectively-diagnosed incident VTE.
Population-based case-control study comparing DVT risk with third-generation vs older OCs. Premenopausal women aged 15-49, includes healthy women without thrombophilia.
Case/non-case and case-control study examining OC-VTE association while assessing bias. Includes women aged 15-49 with suspected VTE, provides valid VT outcome data.
Analysis of PE cases reported during COC treatment. Calculates reporting rates and identifies risk factors for fatal outcome. VT is the primary outcome.
Large prospective cohort study of married women aged 25-39 with VTE as outcome. 105 women with first attack of venous thromboembolism unassociated with pregnancy.
Methodological overview/meta-analysis of meta-analyses comparing RCT and observational study designs. Not primary research on COC-VTE.
Systematic review and meta-analysis summarizing existing evidence. Secondary analysis, not primary research with original patient data.
Prescription event monitoring study evaluating DVT/PE cases in Yasmin users. Reports incidence rate of venous thromboembolism in COC users.
International multicentre case-control study of idiopathic VTE events in relation to combined OC use. 1143 cases aged 20-44 with age-matched controls.
Historical study examining thromboembolic deaths in women of child-bearing age using oral contraceptives. Assesses mortality from VT in COC users.
Cohort and nested case-control study using UK general practice records. Examines VTE risk with different OC preparations in women born 1941-1981.
Case-control study comparing VTE cases with controls, examining third-generation OCs and thrombophilia. 67 cases with VTE compared to 134 controls.
Multicenter case-control study of 425 women with cardiovascular diseases including venous thrombosis. Found significant increase in relative risk of venous thrombosis with OC use.
Randomized trial measuring hemostatic variables (protein C system) rather than clinical VTE outcomes. Mechanistic study without actual VT events as outcome.
Nationwide case-control study focusing on menopausal hormone therapy and VTE risk in pre- and postmenopausal women. Not primarily focused on COC use in healthy reproductive-age women.
Case-control study evaluating VTE risk in women aged 16-44 using second- vs third-generation COCs. Matches population, exposure, and outcome criteria.
Evaluates cardiovascular death including pulmonary embolism in women under 40 using low-estrogen oral contraceptives. Matches criteria.
Methodological review of tools for assessing quality and bias in observational studies. Does not report primary data on COC and VT.

Title indicates a meta-analysis on third-generation OCs and VTE risk. Abstract appears mismatched in the database, but title strongly suggests relevance to COC and VT. Included conservatively for full-text review.
Review article discussing risks and benefits of COCs, including VTE. While a review, it addresses the population and outcome of interest. Included conservatively.
Short commentary/editorial discussing bias in observational studies of OCs and VTE. Does not present primary study data.
Case-control study of fatal VTE in young women (16-39 years) assessing oral contraceptive use as a risk factor. Matches criteria.
Editorial discussing philosophical views of medical science (observational research vs randomized trials). Irrelevant to COC and VT.
Case-control study assessing VTE risk in women aged 15-44 using oral contraceptives, analyzing estrogen dose and progestin type. Matches criteria.
Abstract describes a study on Hepatitis B virus and immune response, completely unrelated to the title or review topic. Irrelevant.
WHO Scientific Group report evaluating data on COC use and cardiovascular disease, including venous thromboembolism. Addresses the review topic. Included conservatively.
Focuses on non-oral contraceptives (injectable DMPA and levonorgestrel IUD) and explicitly excludes oral contraceptive users. Does not meet exposure criteria.
Systematic review and economic evaluation of diagnostic testing strategies for DVT. Does not address COC use or VT risk.
Network meta-analysis of antiplatelet regimens after TIA or stroke. Irrelevant population, exposure, and outcome.
Cohort and nested case-control studies investigating risk factors for idiopathic VTE in women using combined oral contraceptives. Matches criteria.
Case-control study reanalyzing data to assess VTE risk associated with first-time use of second- vs third-generation oral contraceptives. Matches criteria.
Retrospective case-control study examining the relationship between low-estrogen oral contraceptive use and thrombosis. Matches criteria.
Methodological paper simulating attrition in longitudinal data. Irrelevant to COC and VT.
Prospective study investigating pulmonary embolism in women and men, specifically noting increased risk in women using oral contraceptives post-surgery. Addresses COC and VT outcome.
Nested case-control study comparing VTE risk in users of drospirenone-containing vs levonorgestrel-containing COCs. Matches criteria.

This study does not meet the selection criteria for multiple reasons: (1) POPULATION MISMATCH: The study examines hospitalized patients with cardiovascular diseases (peripheral atherosclerotic disease, cerebrovascular disease), not healthy women as required by the selection criteria. (2) INTERVENTION MISMATCH: While 'current estrogen use' is mentioned as one of several independent risk factors, the primary exposure being investigated is cardiovascular diseases, not combined oral contraceptives (COC). The study does not specifically focus on or characterize COC use. (3) STUDY PURPOSE: This is a hospital-based case-control study designed to evaluate cardiovascular diseases as risk factors for VTE, not to assess COC-related VT risk in healthy women. The study explicitly states its purpose is to evaluate 'the effects of major cardiovascular diseases on the risk of VTE.' Therefore, this study clearly does not meet the inclusion criteria.
